description: Cross-vendor dependency matrix showing shared infrastructure and concentration risks.

infrastructure_dependencies.concentration_risk: HIGH - AWS outage in eu-central-1 would simultaneously impact cloud infrastructure AND identity security. 2 of 5 vendors depend on AWS.
infrastructure_dependencies.substitutability: LOW for short-term (weeks), MEDIUM for long-term (months)

infrastructure_dependencies.concentration_risk: MEDIUM - Azure hosts Aladdin, which supports 3 critical functions. No other vendor depends on Azure.
infrastructure_dependencies.substitutability: VERY LOW - Aladdin is tightly coupled to Azure

infrastructure_dependencies.concentration_risk: CRITICAL - 2 critical vendors process data primarily in the US, outside EEA. Potential conflict with bank data residency rule BR-003 and DORA Art. 30(2)(b).
infrastructure_dependencies.substitutability: VERY LOW - no EU-native alternatives for Bloomberg Terminal or Aladdin

single_points_of_failure.risk: CRITICAL - Aladdin unavailability would halt portfolio management, risk measurement, AND fund accounting simultaneously. No alternative platform in place.
HIGH - SWIFT disruption would block trade settlement and payment messaging. However, SWIFT's 99.999% SLA and multi-OPC architecture mitigate this.

hidden_dependency_chains: CyberArk (VND-005) runs on AWS (VND-001). If AWS eu-central-1 fails, both cloud infrastructure AND identity security fail simultaneously.
Aladdin (VND-004) runs on Azure, which runs on Snowflake for analytics. Three layers of dependency for risk calculations.
Bloomberg (VND-002) data feeds through Equinix colocation. Equinix failure could impact both Bloomberg and other co-located services.
